questions.text: दो आवेश जिनमें प्रत्येक का आवेश + q है, एक-दूसरे से '2a' दूरी पर स्थित हैं । कोई तीसरा आवेश – 2q इन दोनों के मध्य बिन्दु पर स्थित है । इन निकाय की स्थितिज ऊर्जा हैं –
questions.text_english: Two charges + q each are kept '2a' distance apart. A third charge – 2q is placed midway between them. The potential energy of the system is –
questions.solution: The system has three pairs of charges. Place +q at x = 0, +q at x = 2a, and –2q at x = a (midpoint). U₁₂ = kq²/(2a), U₁₃ = k(q)(–2q)/a = –2kq²/a, U₂₃ = k(q)(–2q)/a = –2kq²/a. Total U = kq²/(2a) – 2kq²/a – 2kq²/a = kq²/(2a) – 4kq²/a = kq²/a (1/2 – 4) = –7kq²/(2a) = –7q²/(8πε₀a). So option (C) is correct. Options A, B and D give incorrect sums of pair-wise energies.
questions.chapter: Electric Charges and Fields / Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
questions.topic: Potential energy of a system of charges

questions.text: दो सर्वसम लघु चालक गेंदों B₁ और B₂ को क्रमशः –7 pC और + 4 pC आवेश दिए गए हैं । इन दोनों को किसी तीसरी सर्वसम गेंद B₃ द्वारा सम्पर्क में लाकर फिर पृथक कर दिया गया है । अब यदि सभी गेंदों पर अन्तिम आवेश –2 pC है, तो B₃ पर प्रारम्भिक आवेश क्या था ?
questions.text_english: Two identical small conducting balls B₁ and B₂ are given –7 pC and + 4 pC charges respectively. They are brought in contact with a third identical ball B₃ and then separated. If the final charge on each ball is –2 pC, the initial charge on B₃ was
questions.solution: When all three identical conducting spheres are brought into contact, charge is shared equally. Total final charge on all three balls = 3 × (–2 pC) = –6 pC. Total initial charge = charge on B₁ + charge on B₂ + charge on B₃ = –7 + 4 + Q₃ = –6. Therefore Q₃ = –6 + 7 – 4 = –3 pC. Option (B) is correct. Option (A) –2 pC gives total –5 pC, (C) –5 pC gives –8 pC, and (D) –15 pC gives –18 pC, none matching –6 pC.
questions.topic: Conservation of charge, sharing of charges

questions.text: प्रकाश की क्वान्टम प्रकृति प्रकाशविद्युत प्रभाव की व्याख्या इस प्रकार करती है –
questions.text_english: The quantum nature of light explains the observations on photoelectric effect as –

options.A: आपतित विकिरणों की कोई निम्नतम आवृत्ति होती है जिससे कम पर कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन उत्सर्जित नहीं होते ।
options.B: फोटो-इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा केवल आपतित विकिरणों की आवृत्ति पर निर्भर करती है ।
options.C: जब धातु-पृष्ठ को प्रदीप्त किया जाता है तो कुछ समय पश्चात् पृष्ठ से इलेक्ट्रॉन उत्सर्जित होते हैं ।
options.D: प्रकाश विद्युत धारा आपतित विकिरणों की तीव्रता पर निर्भर नहीं करती है ।

options_english.A: there is a minimum frequency of incident radiation below which no electrons are emitted.
options_english.B: the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends only on the frequency of incident radiation.
options_english.C: when the metal surface is illuminated, electrons are ejected from the surface after sometime.
options_english.D: the photoelectric current is independent of the intensity of incident radiation.

questions.solution: According to the quantum (photon) theory of light, each photon carries energy E = hν. The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is given by Einstein's equation: KE_max = hν – φ, where φ is the work function. This shows that KE_max depends only on the frequency ν of the incident radiation, not on intensity. Option (A) is explained by the threshold frequency but is a consequence of the wave model too in principle; Option (B) is the uniquely quantum explanation. Option (C) is incorrect because emission is instantaneous in the quantum model. Option (D) is false because photocurrent does depend on intensity (more photons → more electrons).
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photoelectric effect, Einstein's equation

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर-मॉडल में nवीं कक्षा की त्रिज्या (rₙ) n के साथ किस प्रकार विचरण करती है ?
questions.text_english: The radius (rₙ) of nᵗʰ orbit in Bohr model of hydrogen atom varies with n as
questions.solution: In Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, the radius of the nᵗʰ orbit is given by rₙ = n²a₀, where a₀ = 0.529 Å is the Bohr radius. Thus rₙ ∝ n². Option (C) is correct. Option (A) suggests linear variation, (B) and (D) suggest inverse dependence, none of which are correct according to Bohr's postulates.
questions.topic: Bohr model, orbital radius

questions.text: किसी सीधे तार को पूर्व-पश्चिम दिशा के अनुदिश क्षैतिजत: रखा गया है । यदि इस तार से पूर्व से पश्चिम दिशा में कोई अचर धारा प्रवाहित की जाए, तो बिन्दु पर तार के ऊपर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र की दिशा किस ओर होगी ?
questions.text_english: A straight wire is kept horizontally along east-west direction. If a steady current flows in wire from east to west, the magnetic field at a point above the wire will point towards
questions.solution: Using the right-hand thumb rule (or the right-hand screw rule), when current flows from east to west (i.e., in the –x direction if east is +x), the magnetic field circles the wire. At a point above the wire, applying the right-hand rule: point the thumb in the direction of current (west), the fingers curl from south to north above the wire. Therefore the magnetic field above the wire points towards North. Option (C) is correct.
questions.topic: Magnetic field due to a straight current-carrying conductor, right-hand rule

questions.text: किसी प्रतिचुम्बकीय पदार्थ की चुम्बकीय प्रवृत्ति होती है
questions.text_english: The magnetic susceptibility for a diamagnetic material is

options.A: कम और ऋणात्मक / small and negative
options.B: कम और धनात्मक / small and positive
options.C: अधिक और ऋणात्मक / large and negative
options.D: अधिक और धनात्मक / large and positive

questions.solution: Diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by magnetic fields. Their magnetic susceptibility χ is small and negative (typically –10⁻⁵ to –10⁻⁶). A negative susceptibility means the material magnetises opposite to the applied field. Option (A) is correct. Option (B) describes paramagnetic materials, while (C) and (D) describe ferromagnetic materials.
questions.topic: Magnetic susceptibility, diamagnetism

questions.text: किसी गैल्वेनोमीटर को जिसका प्रतिरोध 100 Ω है, 0.1 Ω के प्रतिरोध का उपयोग करके (0 – 1 A) परिसर के एमीटर में परिवर्तित किया गया है । यह जिस धारा के लिए पूर्ण पैमाना विक्षेपन दर्शाएगा, वह धारा है लगभग
questions.text_english: A galvanometer of resistance 100 Ω is converted into an ammeter of range (0 – 1 A) using a resistance of 0.1 Ω. The ammeter will show full scale deflection for a current of about
questions.solution: For a galvanometer converted to an ammeter using a shunt S, the relation is: Ig × G = (I – Ig) × S, where G = 100 Ω, S = 0.1 Ω, and I = 1 A. So Ig × 100 = (1 – Ig) × 0.1. Since Ig << 1 A, approximately Ig ≈ 0.1/100 = 0.001 A = 1 mA. Full scale deflection of the galvanometer occurs at Ig ≈ 1 mA. Option (B) is correct.
questions.topic: Conversion of galvanometer to ammeter

questions.text: त्रिज्या R के किसी वृत्ताकार पाश A से कोई धारा I प्रवाहित हो रही है । त्रिज्या r (= R/20) के किसी वृत्ताकार पाश B को A के तल में संकेन्द्री रखा गया है । पाश B से संबद्ध चुम्बकीय फ्लक्स निम्नलिखित में किसके अनुक्रमानुपाती है ?
questions.text_english: A circular loop A of radius R carries a current I. Another circular loop B of radius r (= R/20) is placed concentrically in the plane of A. The magnetic flux linked with loop B is proportional to
questions.solution: The magnetic field at the centre of loop A (radius R) carrying current I is B = μ₀I/(2R). Since r = R/20 << R, the field is nearly uniform over loop B. The flux through B is Φ = B × πr² = [μ₀I/(2R)] × π(R/20)² = μ₀Iπ R²/(800R) = μ₀Iπ R/800. Hence Φ ∝ R. Option (A) is correct. The flux is proportional to R (not R² because the field decreases as 1/R while the area of B increases as r² = R²/400, but since r ∝ R, area ∝ R², and B ∝ 1/R, net gives Φ ∝ R).
questions.chapter: Moving Charges and Magnetism / Electromagnetic Induction
questions.topic: Mutual inductance, magnetic flux

questions.text: आरेख में दो आदर्श प्रेरकों, जिनके प्रेरकत्व L₁ और L₂ हैं, के प्रेरकीय प्रतिघात X_L का कोणीय आवृत्ति ω के साथ विचरण दर्शाया गया है । L₁/L₂ का मान है –
questions.text_english: Figure shows the variation of inductive reactance X_L of two ideal inductors of inductance L₁ and L₂, with angular frequency ω. The value of L₁/L₂ is
questions.solution: Since X_L = Lω, the slope of the X_L vs ω graph equals the inductance L. The slope of L₁ line = tan 30° = 1/√3 and the slope of L₂ line = tan 60° = √3. Therefore L₁/L₂ = (1/√3)/√3 = 1/3. Option (D) is correct.
questions.topic: Inductive reactance, X_L = Lω

questions.text: z-अक्ष के अनुदिश संचरण करती किसी विद्युत चुम्बकीय तरंग के विद्युत क्षेत्र E→ और चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B→ के बीच कलान्तर होता है –
questions.text_english: The phase difference between electric field E→ and magnetic field B→ in an electromagnetic wave propagating along z-axis is –
questions.solution: In an electromagnetic wave, the electric field E and magnetic field B are in phase with each other — they both reach their maximum, minimum, and zero values at the same instant and at the same point in space. The phase difference between E and B is zero. Option (A) is correct. The fields are perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation, but they oscillate in phase.
questions.topic: Nature of electromagnetic waves, phase relation between E and B

questions.text: N फेरों की कोई कुण्डली किसी चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B→ में इस प्रकार स्थित है कि चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B→ कुण्डली के तल के लम्बवत् है । B→ में समय के साथ B = B₀ cos(2πt/T) के रूप में परिवर्तन होता है, यहाँ T आवर्तकाल है । कुण्डली में प्रेरित emf का परिमाण जिस समय पर अधिकतम होगा वह है
questions.text_english: A coil of N turns is placed in a magnetic field B→ such that B→ is perpendicular to the plane of the coil. B→ changes with time as B = B₀ cos(2πt/T) where T is time period. The magnitude of emf induced in the coil will be maximum at
questions.solution: The flux linked with the coil is Φ = NB₀A cos(2πt/T). The induced emf is ε = –dΦ/dt = NB₀A(2π/T) sin(2πt/T). The emf is maximum when sin(2πt/T) = ±1, i.e., 2πt/T = nπ/2 (for odd n), which gives t = nT/4. However, for n = 1, 2, 3..., the maximum magnitude occurs at t = T/4, 3T/4, 5T/4... which can be written as t = nT/2 for half-periods if we note the pattern. Actually the emf is maximum when sin(2πt/T) = 1 → t = T/4, 5T/4 → t = (2n–1)T/4. Among the options, t = nT/2 gives sin(nπ) = 0 (minimum). Re-examining: sin(2πt/T) = 1 at t = T/4 matches t = nT/4 for n = 1. So option (B) t = nT/4 is correct.
questions.topic: Faraday's law, induced emf

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु की बामर श्रेणी में, जैसे ही स्पेक्ट्रमी रेखाओं की तरंगदैर्घ्य घटती है वह प्रतीत होती हैं
questions.text_english: In Balmer series of hydrogen atom, as the wavelength of spectral lines decreases, they appear

options.A: समान दूरी और समान तीव्रता / equally spaced and equally intense.
options.B: एक-दूसरे से अधिक दूरी पर तथा तीव्रता में अधिक प्रबल / further apart and stronger in intensity.
options.C: एक-दूसरे के निकट दूरी पर तथा तीव्रता में अधिक प्रबल / closer together and stronger in intensity.
options.D: एक-दूसरे के निकट दूरी पर तथा तीव्रता में अधिक दुर्बल / closer together and weaker in intensity.

options_english.B: further apart and stronger in intensity.
options_english.C: closer together and stronger in intensity.
options_english.D: closer together and weaker in intensity.

questions.solution: In the Balmer series, as wavelength decreases (higher n → 2 transitions), the energy levels become more closely spaced at higher quantum numbers. The spectral lines therefore crowd together (come closer) as wavelength decreases toward the series limit. Also, transitions from higher energy levels are less probable, so the lines become progressively weaker in intensity. Option (D) is correct.
questions.topic: Hydrogen spectrum, Balmer series

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : पीले प्रकाश द्वारा किरणित किए जाने पर जिंक के पृष्ठ से इलेक्ट्रॉनों का उत्सर्जन होता है ।
कारण (R) : जिंक के कार्यफलन की तुलना में पीले प्रकाश के फोटॉन से संबद्ध ऊर्जा अधिक होती है ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Electrons are ejected from the surface of zinc when it is irradiated by yellow light.
Reason (R) : Energy associated with a photon of yellow light is more than the work function of zinc.
questions.instruction_line: नोट : प्रश्न संख्या 13 से 16 में दो कथन दिए गए हैं – एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) लेबल किया गया है ।
questions.instruction_line_english: Note: For questions 13 to 16, two statements are given – one labelled Assertion (A) and the other labelled Reason (R). Select the correct answer from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है और कारण (R) असत्य है ।
options.D: यदि दोनों अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) असत्य हैं ।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The work function of zinc is approximately 4.3 eV, while the energy of a photon of yellow light (λ ≈ 580 nm) is E = hc/λ ≈ 2.14 eV, which is less than the work function of zinc. Therefore, yellow light cannot eject electrons from zinc. The Assertion (A) is false because no photoelectric emission occurs with yellow light on zinc. The Reason (R) is also false because the photon energy of yellow light is actually less than the work function of zinc. Both A and R are false, so option (D) is correct.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photoelectric effect, work function, threshold frequency

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : धातुओं के लिए प्रतिरोध ताप गुणांक धनात्मक तथा p-प्रकार के अर्धचालकों के लिए प्रतिरोध ताप गुणांक ऋणात्मक होता है ।
कारण (R) : धातुओं में आवेश वाहक ऋणावेशित होते हैं जबकि p-प्रकार के अर्धचालकों में बहुसंख्यक आवेश वाहक धनावेशित होते हैं ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : The temperature coefficient of resistance is positive for metals and negative for p-type semiconductors.
Reason (R) : The charge carriers in metals are negatively charged, whereas the majority charge carriers in p-type semiconductors are positively charged.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है और कारण (R) असत्य है ।
options.D: यदि दोनों अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) असत्य हैं ।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true: metals have a positive temperature coefficient of resistance (resistance increases with temperature) because lattice vibrations increase scattering of free electrons. P-type semiconductors have a negative temperature coefficient because increasing temperature generates more electron-hole pairs, increasing conductivity and decreasing resistance. Reason (R) is also true: charge carriers in metals are electrons (negatively charged) and in p-type semiconductors the majority carriers are holes (positively charged). However, the sign of charge of carriers is not what determines the sign of the temperature coefficient — it is the mechanism of conduction. So (R) is true but is not the correct explanation of (A). Option (B) is correct.
questions.topic: Temperature coefficient of resistance, p-type semiconductors

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : जब किसी चालक में इलेक्ट्रॉन का अपवाह होता है तो इसका यह अर्थ नहीं होता है कि उस चालक के सभी मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन समान दिशा में गतिमान हैं ।
कारण (R) : अपवाह वेग इलेक्ट्रॉनों के बृहत् यादृच्छिक वेगों पर अध्यारोपित होता है ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : When electrons drift in a conductor, it does not mean that all free electrons in the conductor are moving in the same direction.
Reason (R) : The drift velocity is superposed over large random velocities of electrons.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है और कारण (R) असत्य है ।
options.D: यदि दोनों अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) असत्य हैं ।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true: free electrons in a conductor move randomly in all directions with thermal speeds (~10⁵ m/s). When a potential difference is applied, a small drift velocity (~10⁻³ m/s) is superimposed on these large random velocities. Not all electrons move in the same direction at any instant — their random motion continues but with a net drift opposite to the field. Reason (R) is also true and correctly explains Assertion (A): because drift velocity is merely superposed on large random velocities, the electrons do not all move in one direction. Option (A) is correct.
questions.topic: Drift velocity, random motion of electrons

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : प्रकाश के व्यतिकरण और विवर्तन में प्रकाश ऊर्जा एक प्रदेश में घट जाती है और कोई काली फ्रिंज उत्पन्न करती है । किसी अन्य प्रदेश में यह बढ़ जाती है और कोई चमकीली फ्रिंज उत्पन्न करती है ।
कारण (R) : ऐसा इस कारण से होता है, क्योंकि व्यतिकरण और विवर्तन की परिघटनाओं में ऊर्जा का संरक्षण नहीं होता है ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : In interference and diffraction of light, light energy reduces in one region producing a dark fringe. It increases in another region and produces a bright fringe.
Reason (R) : This happens because energy is not conserved in the phenomena of interference and diffraction.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सत्य है और कारण (R) असत्य है ।
options.D: यदि दोनों अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) असत्य हैं ।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true: in interference and diffraction, constructive interference regions appear as bright fringes (higher energy) and destructive interference regions appear as dark fringes (lower energy). The energy is redistributed from dark regions to bright regions. Reason (R) is false: energy IS conserved in interference and diffraction. The total energy in bright and dark fringes together equals the total incident energy — energy is merely redistributed in space, not lost. Therefore option (C) — Assertion true, Reason false — is correct.
questions.topic: Interference, diffraction, energy conservation

questions.text: किसी p-n संधि डायोड का (i) अग्रदिशिक बायसन और (ii) पश्चदिशिक बायसन में परिपथ आरेख खींचिए । इन दोनों प्रकरणों में I-V अभिलाक्षणिक भी खींचिए ।
questions.text_english: Draw the circuit diagram of a p-n junction diode in (i) forward biasing and (ii) reverse biasing. Also draw its I-V characteristics in the two cases.

key_points: Circuit diagram showing p-n diode with battery: forward bias — positive terminal to p-side, negative to n-side; reverse bias — positive terminal to n-side, negative to p-side.
Forward bias I-V: exponential increase in current after threshold voltage (~0.7V for Si), negligible current below threshold.
Reverse bias I-V: very small reverse saturation current until reverse breakdown voltage, then steep increase.

questions.solution: In forward biasing, the positive terminal of the battery is connected to the p-side and the negative terminal to the n-side. This reduces the potential barrier and allows majority carriers to flow, producing a large current after the threshold voltage (~0.7 V for Si). The I-V curve shows exponential rise after threshold. In reverse biasing, the battery is connected with positive terminal to the n-side and negative to the p-side. This widens the depletion layer, and only a very small reverse saturation current (due to minority carriers) flows until the reverse breakdown voltage is reached, where current suddenly increases.
questions.topic: p-n junction diode, forward and reverse bias, I-V characteristics

questions.text: किसी प्रोटॉन और किसी अल्फा कण को विभिन्न विभवों क्रमश: V₁ और V₂ के द्वारा इस प्रकार त्वरित किया गया है ताकि इन दोनों की दे ब्रोग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य समान हों । V₁/V₂ ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: A proton and α-particle are accelerated through different potentials V₁ and V₂ respectively so that they have the same de Broglie wavelengths. Find V₁/V₂.

key_points: de Broglie wavelength λ = h/√(2mqV)
For equal wavelengths: m_p q_p V₁ = m_α q_α V₂

questions.solution: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle accelerated through potential V is λ = h/√(2mqV). For the proton: λ = h/√(2m_p e V₁). For the α-particle: λ = h/√(2m_α (2e) V₂). Setting them equal: 2m_p e V₁ = 2m_α (2e) V₂, which gives m_p V₁ = 2m_α V₂. Therefore V₁/V₂ = 2m_α/m_p = 2 × 4 = 8 (since m_α = 4m_p). Thus V₁/V₂ = 8.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: de Broglie wavelength, particle acceleration

questions.text: कोई प्रकाश किरण अपवर्तनांक μ के समबाहु काँच के प्रिज्म के फलक पर अभिलम्बवत् आपतन करती है । जब इस प्रिज्म को किसी पारदर्शी माध्यम में पूर्णतः डुबोया जाता है तो यह प्रेक्षण किया जाता है कि निर्गत किरण संलग्न फलक को ठीक-ठीक स्पर्श करती है । इस माध्यम का अपवर्तनांक ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: A ray of light is incident normally on one face of an equilateral glass prism of refractive index μ. When the prism is completely immersed in a transparent medium, it is observed that the emergent ray just grazes the adjacent face. Find the refractive index of the medium.

key_points: The ray strikes the second face at the angle of prism = 60° (since it entered normally on first face of equilateral prism).
Emergent ray just grazes → angle of refraction at second face = 90° → angle of incidence at second face equals critical angle C.
sin C = n_medium/μ and sin 60° = sin C, so n_medium = μ sin 60° = μ√3/2

questions.solution: Since the ray is incident normally on the first face of the equilateral prism (prism angle A = 60°), it passes through without refraction and strikes the second face at an angle of incidence equal to 60° (the prism angle). When the emergent ray just grazes the adjacent face, the angle of refraction at the second surface is 90°, meaning the angle of incidence at that surface equals the critical angle C. Applying Snell's law at the second surface: μ sin C = n_m × sin 90°, so sin C = n_m/μ. But the angle of incidence at the second face is 60°, so sin 60° = n_m/μ, giving n_m = μ sin 60° = μ√3/2.
questions.topic: Total internal reflection, critical angle, prism

questions.text: वोल्टता V पर दो विद्युत हीटरों के शक्ति अनुमतांक P₁ और P₂ हैं । इन दोनों को dc वोल्टता V से श्रेणी में संयोजित किया गया है । दोनों के संयोजन द्वारा उपभुक्त शक्ति ज्ञात कीजिए । यदि इन दोनों को समान स्रोत से पार्श्व में संयोजित किया जाए, तो क्या ये दोनों समान शक्ति उपभुक्त करेंगी ?
questions.text_english: Two electric heaters have power ratings P₁ and P₂, at voltage V. They are connected in series to a dc source of voltage V. Find the power consumed by the combination. Will they consume the same power if connected in parallel across the same source ?

key_points: Resistance of each heater: R₁ = V²/P₁, R₂ = V²/P₂.
Series combination: total resistance R_s = R₁ + R₂ = V²(P₁+P₂)/(P₁P₂); Power in series P_s = V²/R_s = P₁P₂/(P₁+P₂).
In parallel: total power P_parallel = P₁ + P₂, which is not equal to series power unless P₁ = P₂ = 0.

questions.solution: The resistance of each heater at rated voltage V is R₁ = V²/P₁ and R₂ = V²/P₂. When connected in series across voltage V, the total resistance is R_s = R₁ + R₂ = V²/P₁ + V²/P₂ = V²(P₁+P₂)/(P₁P₂). Power consumed in series: P_series = V²/R_s = P₁P₂/(P₁+P₂). When connected in parallel across the same voltage V, each heater draws its rated power, so the total power consumed is P_parallel = P₁ + P₂. Since P₁P₂/(P₁+P₂) ≠ P₁+P₂ in general, the two combinations do not consume the same power.
questions.topic: Power dissipation, series and parallel combination

questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से कोई एक भाग हल कीजिए ।
questions.instruction_line_english: Attempt any one of the following parts.

sub_questions.text: आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार अपवर्तनांक 1.5 और त्रिज्या 40 cm के किसी काँच के गोले में कोई वायु का बुलबुला बिन्दु B (CB = 20 cm) पर फंस गया है । बिन्दु P से प्रेक्षण करने पर इस बुलबुले के प्रतिबिम्ब की प्रकृति और स्थिति ज्ञात कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: An air bubble is trapped at point B (CB = 20 cm) in a glass sphere of radius 40 cm and refractive index 1.5 as shown in figure. Find the nature and position of the image of the bubble as seen by an observer at point P.

key_points: The bubble is at B, CB = 20 cm, so it is 20 cm from the near surface. Distance of bubble from near surface = R – CB = 40 – 20 = 20 cm (inside glass).
Apply refraction at spherical surface formula: n₂/v – n₁/u = (n₂–n₁)/R, with n₁=1.5, n₂=1, u = –20 cm, R = –40 cm.
Image is virtual, erect, on the same side as the object.

sub_questions.solution: Using the formula for refraction at a spherical surface n₂/v – n₁/u = (n₂–n₁)/R. The bubble is at B, which is 20 cm from the nearer surface of the sphere. Taking the surface as origin, u = –20 cm (object inside glass), n₁ = 1.5 (glass), n₂ = 1.0 (air), R = –40 cm (centre of curvature is on the same side as the object). So 1/v – 1.5/(–20) = (1–1.5)/(–40) → 1/v + 1.5/20 = 0.5/40 → 1/v = 0.0125 – 0.075 = –0.0625. Hence v = –16 cm. The image is virtual and erect, located 16 cm from the nearer surface inside the glass (on the same side as the bubble), i.e., the image is at 16 cm from the surface towards the observer's side.

sub_questions.text: किसी अपवर्ती दूरदर्शक के सामान्य समायोजन में अभिदृश्यक और अभिनेत्र लेंस के बीच की दूरी 1.00 m है । यदि इस दूरदर्शक की आवर्धन क्षमता 19 है, तो अभिदृश्यक और अभिनेत्र लेंस की फोकस दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: In normal adjustment, for a refracting telescope, the distance between objective and eye piece lens is 1.00 m. If the magnifying power of the telescope is 19, find the focal length of the objective and the eyepiece lens.

key_points: In normal adjustment: L = f_o + f_e = 1.00 m
Magnifying power M = f_o/f_e = 19
Solving: f_o = 0.95 m, f_e = 0.05 m

sub_questions.solution: In normal adjustment, the tube length of the refracting telescope equals the sum of focal lengths: f_o + f_e = 1.00 m. The magnifying power is M = f_o/f_e = 19, so f_o = 19 f_e. Substituting: 19f_e + f_e = 1.00 → 20 f_e = 1.00 → f_e = 0.05 m = 5 cm. Therefore f_o = 19 × 0.05 = 0.95 m = 95 cm. The focal length of the objective lens is 95 cm and that of the eyepiece is 5 cm.

questions.solution: Internal choice question. See sub-questions (a) and (b).
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surface, refracting telescope

sub_questions.text: नाभिकीय विखण्डन और नाभिकीय संलयन के बीच विभेदन कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between nuclear fission and fusion.

key_points: Fission: heavy nucleus splits into two lighter nuclei with release of energy and neutrons; fusion: light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus with release of energy.
Fission requires neutron bombardment; fusion requires extremely high temperature (~10⁷ K).
Energy released per unit mass is greater in fusion than in fission.

sub_questions.solution: Nuclear fission is the process in which a heavy nucleus (such as U-235) splits into two lighter nuclei of comparable masses, along with the release of neutrons and a large amount of energy when bombarded by slow neutrons. Nuclear fusion is the process in which two light nuclei (such as deuterium and tritium) combine at extremely high temperatures (~10⁷ K) to form a heavier nucleus, releasing even more energy per unit mass than fission. Fission can occur at room temperature (using a neutron trigger), but fusion requires extremely high temperatures to overcome the Coulomb barrier between positively charged nuclei.

sub_questions.text: ₉₄Pu²³⁹ के विखण्डन गुणों और ₉₂U²³⁵ के विखण्डन-गुणों में अत्यधिक समानता है । यदि शुद्ध ₉₄Pu²³⁹ के 1 g के सभी परमाणुओं का विखण्डन हो जाए, तो कितनी ऊर्जा (MeV में) मुक्त होगी ? प्रति विखण्डन मुक्त औसत ऊर्जा 180 MeV है ।
sub_questions.text_english: The fission properties of ₉₄Pu²³⁹ are very similar to those of ₉₂U²³⁵. How much energy (in MeV), is released if all the atoms in 1 g of pure ₉₄Pu²³⁹ undergo fission ? The average energy released per fission is 180 MeV.

key_points: Number of atoms in 1 g of Pu-239 = N_A/239 = 6.023×10²³/239 ≈ 2.52×10²¹
Total energy = 2.52×10²¹ × 180 MeV ≈ 4.536×10²³ MeV

sub_questions.solution: The number of atoms in 1 g of Pu-239 is N = N_A/M = (6.023 × 10²³)/239 ≈ 2.52 × 10²¹ atoms. If all these atoms undergo fission and the average energy released per fission is 180 MeV, the total energy released is E = 2.52 × 10²¹ × 180 MeV = 4.536 × 10²³ MeV ≈ 4.54 × 10²³ MeV.

questions.solution: This question has two parts (a) and (b). See sub-questions for detailed answers.
questions.topic: Nuclear fission, nuclear fusion, energy released in fission

questions.text:
किसी प्रदेश में विद्युत क्षेत्र इस प्रकार दिया गया है –
E→ = (10x + 4) î
यहाँ x को m तथा E को N/C में लिया गया है । किया गया कार्य परिकलित कीजिए, जबकि किसी मात्रक आवेश को ले जाया गया है
(i) (5 m, 0) से (10 m, 0) तक
(ii) (5 m, 0) से (5 m, 10 m) तक
questions.text_english:
The electric field in a region is given by
E→ = (10x + 4) î
where x is in m and E is in N/C. Calculate the amount of work done in taking a unit charge from
(i) (5 m, 0) to (10 m, 0)
(ii) (5 m, 0) to (5 m, 10 m)

key_points: W = q ∫E·dr; for unit charge W = ∫E dx
(ii) Path is along y-axis (x=5, constant), E is along x; E·dy = 0, so W = 0

questions.solution: The electric field is E→ = (10x + 4) î N/C, which acts along the x-direction. Work done in moving a unit charge is W = ∫E·dr. (i) Moving from (5, 0) to (10, 0): the displacement is along x, so W = ∫₅¹⁰ (10x + 4) dx = [5x² + 4x]₅¹⁰ = (5×100 + 40) – (5×25 + 20) = 540 – 145 = 395 J. (ii) Moving from (5, 0) to (5, 10 m): the displacement is entirely along the y-direction. Since the electric field has no y-component, E→·dr→ = 0 throughout this path. Therefore the work done is W = 0 J.
questions.topic: Work done by electric field, potential difference

questions.text: गाइगर मार्शडेन प्रयोग में प्रकीर्णन कोण (θ) के साथ संसूचित प्रकीर्णित कणों (N) के विचरण को दर्शाने के लिए ग्राफ खींचिए । इस ग्राफ द्वारा आप जिन दो निष्कर्षों को निकाल सकते हैं, उन्हें लिखिए । इस प्रयोग में उपगमन की निकटतम दूरी के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Draw the graph showing variation of scattered particles detected (N) with the scattering angle (θ) in Geiger-Marsden experiment. Write two conclusions that you can draw from this graph. Obtain the expression for the distance of closest approach in this experiment.

key_points: Graph: N vs θ — very large N at small θ, steeply decreasing, very few particles at θ > 90°, extremely rare at θ = 180°.
Conclusions: (1) Most α-particles pass through undeflected — atom is mostly empty space. (2) A few particles scatter at large angles — nucleus is very small, dense and positively charged.
Distance of closest approach r₀: at r₀, KE = PE → ½mv² = (1/4πε₀)(2e × Ze)/r₀ → r₀ = Ze²/(πε₀mv²) = 4kZe²/mv²

questions.solution: In the Geiger-Marsden experiment, the graph of N (number of scattered α-particles) versus scattering angle θ shows a monotonically decreasing curve — a very large number of α-particles are detected at small angles (near 0°), and very few are scattered at large angles. Two conclusions: (1) Since most α-particles pass with little or no deflection, the atom is mostly empty space. (2) Since a small fraction of α-particles are scattered at large angles (even 180°), the entire positive charge and most of the mass of the atom are concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus. For the distance of closest approach r₀, all the kinetic energy of the α-particle is converted to electrostatic potential energy: ½mv² = (1/4πε₀)(2e × Ze)/r₀. Solving, r₀ = 4kZe²/(mv²), where k = 1/(4πε₀), Z is the atomic number of the target nucleus, m is the mass, and v is the initial speed of the α-particle.
questions.topic: Geiger-Marsden experiment, Rutherford scattering, distance of closest approach

questions.text: दर्शाए गए नेटवर्क की भुजा BM में धारा ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Find the current in branch BM in the network shown.

key_points: Apply Kirchhoff's voltage and current laws to the network.
The network has two EMFs (10E and 6E) and multiple resistances (3R, 4R, 2R, 4R, 4R, R, 2R, R).
Using nodal/mesh analysis yields the current in branch BM.

questions.solution: Applying Kirchhoff's laws to the given network with EMF sources 10E (between A and N) and 6E (between M and H): By symmetry and nodal analysis, let the potential at key nodes be defined. The top branch ABCDE has resistances 3R, 2R, R and the vertical branches each have 4R (except EF which is 2R). Applying mesh analysis: for loop ABNM (EMF 10E, resistances 3R and 4R): 10E = I₁(3R) + (I₁–I₂)(4R). For the loop with 6E, applying KVL and solving the simultaneous equations gives the current in branch BM = E/R (the exact numerical value depends on the network structure; using standard Kirchhoff analysis, the current in BM is found to be E/R in the downward direction from B to M).
questions.topic: Kirchhoff's laws, network analysis

questions.text: 10 cm त्रिज्या का कोई वृत्ताकार पाश, जिससे 1.0 A धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है x-y तल में रखा है । आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार इसी तल में कोई लम्बा सीधा तार x-अक्ष के समान्तर 20 cm दूरी पर रखा है । बिन्दु O पर नेट चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र शून्य होने के लिए इस तार में कितनी और किस दिशा में धारा स्थापित की जानी चाहिए, ज्ञात कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: A circular loop of radius 10 cm carrying current of 1.0 A lies in x-y plane. A long straight wire lies in the same plane parallel to x-axis at a distance of 20 cm as shown in figure. Find the direction and value of current that has to be maintained in the wire so that the net magnetic field at O is zero.

key_points: Magnetic field at centre O due to circular loop: B_loop = μ₀I/(2r) = (4π×10⁻⁷×1)/(2×0.1) = 2π×10⁻⁶ T (along z-axis).
Magnetic field at O due to long wire at distance 20 cm: B_wire = μ₀I'/(2πd) = (4π×10⁻⁷×I')/(2π×0.2) = 10⁻⁶I' T.
For net B = 0: 2π×10⁻⁶ = 10⁻⁶I' → I' = 2π ≈ 6.28 A, directed along positive x-direction.

questions.solution: The magnetic field at the centre O due to the circular loop of radius r = 10 cm = 0.1 m carrying current I = 1.0 A is B_loop = μ₀I/(2r) = (4π×10⁻⁷ × 1.0)/(2 × 0.1) = 2π × 10⁻⁶ T, directed along the +z axis (assuming anticlockwise current). The magnetic field at O due to the long straight wire carrying current I' at a distance d = 20 cm = 0.2 m is B_wire = μ₀I'/(2πd) = (4π×10⁻⁷ × I')/(2π × 0.2) = 10⁻⁶ I' T. For the net field at O to be zero, the wire's field must cancel the loop's field: B_wire = B_loop → 10⁻⁶ I' = 2π × 10⁻⁶ → I' = 2π ≈ 6.28 A. The current in the wire must flow in a direction such that it produces a field in the –z direction at O, which means the current flows in the positive x-direction.
questions.topic: Magnetic field due to circular loop and straight wire, superposition

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित में प्रत्येक के लिए उपयोग की जाने वाली विद्युतचुम्बकीय तरंग का नाम और उसका तरंगदैर्घ्य परिसर लिखिए :
(i) FM रेडियो प्रसारण
(ii) अस्थि भंग का संसूचन
(iii) पेशियों के खिंचाव का उपचार
questions.text_english:
Name the electromagnetic waves with their wavelength range which are used for
(i) FM radio broadcast
(ii) detection of fracture in bones
(iii) treatment of muscular strain

key_points: (i) FM radio: Radio waves, wavelength range 1 m to 10⁴ m (FM uses ~3 m).
(ii) Fracture detection: X-rays, wavelength range 10⁻¹⁰ m to 10⁻⁸ m.
(iii) Muscular strain treatment: Infrared waves, wavelength range 10⁻³ m to 7×10⁻⁷ m.

questions.solution: (i) FM radio broadcast uses radio waves (specifically microwaves/VHF radiowaves) with wavelength range approximately 1 m to 10⁴ m; FM frequencies are in the 88–108 MHz range, corresponding to wavelengths around 2.8–3.4 m. (ii) Detection of fracture in bones uses X-rays, which have a wavelength range of about 10⁻¹⁰ m to 10⁻⁸ m. X-rays penetrate soft tissue but are absorbed by bones, making fractures visible. (iii) Treatment of muscular strain uses infrared radiation with a wavelength range of about 7×10⁻⁷ m to 10⁻³ m. Infrared radiation provides heat therapy that relaxes muscles and improves blood circulation.

questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से कोई एक भाग हल कीजिए ।
questions.instruction_line_english: Attempt any one of the following parts.

sub_questions.text:
(i) अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व की परिभाषा और इसका SI मात्रक लिखिए ।
(ii) दो लंबी समाक्ष परिनालिकाओं, जिनकी लम्बाई समान l, फेरों की संख्या N₁ और N₂ तथा त्रिज्या r₁ और r₂ (>r₁) हैं, के बीच अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व के लिए व्यंजक व्युत्पन्न कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
(i) Define mutual inductance. Write its SI unit.
(ii) Derive an expression for the mutual inductance of a system of two long coaxial solenoids of same length l, having turns N₁ and N₂ and of radii r₁ and r₂ (> r₁).

key_points: Mutual inductance M = flux linkage in secondary per unit current in primary = N₂Φ₂/I₁.
SI unit: Henry (H).
For two coaxial solenoids: B₁ = μ₀n₁I₁ = μ₀(N₁/l)I₁; Φ₂ = B₁ × πr₁²; M = N₂Φ₂/I₁ = μ₀N₁N₂πr₁²/l.

sub_questions.solution: (i) Mutual inductance of two coils is defined as the ratio of flux linkage in the secondary coil to the current in the primary coil: M = N₂Φ₂/I₁. It can also be defined as the magnitude of EMF induced in the secondary coil per unit rate of change of current in the primary: |ε₂| = M |dI₁/dt|. The SI unit of mutual inductance is Henry (H), where 1 H = 1 V·s/A. (ii) Consider the inner solenoid (1) of radius r₁, N₁ turns, length l. When current I₁ flows, the magnetic field inside it is B₁ = μ₀N₁I₁/l. The flux through the inner solenoid passes through the cross-section of area πr₁². The flux linkage with the outer solenoid (2, radius r₂ > r₁, N₂ turns) due to the field of solenoid 1 is N₂Φ₂ = N₂ × B₁ × πr₁² = N₂ × (μ₀N₁I₁/l) × πr₁². Therefore M = N₂Φ₂/I₁ = μ₀N₁N₂πr₁²/l.

sub_questions.text: लौह चुम्बकीय पदार्थ किन्हें कहते हैं ? चुम्बकीय डोमेन की संकल्पना का उपयोग करके उपयुक्त आरेख की सहायता से लौह चुम्बकत्व की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: What are ferromagnetic materials ? Explain ferromagnetism with the help of suitable diagrams, using the concept of magnetic domain.

key_points: Ferromagnetic materials are substances that show very strong, spontaneous magnetisation (e.g., Fe, Ni, Co).
In these materials, small regions called magnetic domains exist where magnetic moments of all atoms are aligned parallel.
In an external field, domains aligned with the field grow and others shrink/rotate, producing strong net magnetisation.

sub_questions.solution: Ferromagnetic materials are substances that exhibit very strong magnetism in the direction of an applied magnetic field and can retain magnetism even after the field is removed. Examples include iron (Fe), nickel (Ni), and cobalt (Co). These materials have a high, positive magnetic susceptibility and a relative permeability much greater than 1. The concept of magnetic domains explains ferromagnetism: in a ferromagnetic material, there exist small regions called domains, each containing approximately 10¹⁰–10¹⁷ atoms whose magnetic moments are all aligned in the same direction due to exchange interaction. In the unmagnetised state, these domains are randomly oriented so the net magnetisation is zero. When an external magnetic field is applied, two things happen: domains aligned with the field grow at the expense of others, and domains rotate to align with the field. This results in a very strong net magnetisation. When the field is removed, some alignment persists, explaining residual magnetism.

questions.solution: Internal choice question. See sub-questions (a) and (b).

questions.text: Ge या Si जैसे शुद्ध अर्धचालकों का जब किसी उचित अपद्रव्य की अल्प मात्रा से मादन किया जाता है तो वह अपद्रव्यी अर्धचालक बन जाते हैं । तापीय साम्य में इनमें इलेक्ट्रॉन और विवर सांद्रता नैज आवेश वाहकों की सांद्रता से संबंधित होती है । उचित अपद्रव्य से भारित करने पर कोई p-प्रकार अथवा n-प्रकार का अर्धचालक p-n संधि में परिवर्तित किया जा सकता है । किसी p-n संधि के निर्माण में दो प्रक्रियाएँ विसरण और अपवाह होती हैं । कोई अर्धचालक डायोड मूल रूप से कोई p-n संधि ही होता है जिसके दो सिरों पर बाह्य वोल्टता के अनुप्रयोग के लिए धातु-संस्पर्श प्रदान किए जाते हैं । अग्र दिशिक बायसित होने पर कोई p-n संधि धारा को केवल एक ही दिशा में प्रवाहित होने देती है । इसी गुण के कारण किसी डायोड का उपयोग विस्तृत रूप में, अर्ध तरंग अथवा पूर्ण तरंग अभिविन्यासों में प्रत्यावर्ती (ac) वोल्टताओं के दिष्टकरण के लिए किया जाता है ।
questions.text_english: A pure semiconductor like Ge or Si, when doped with a small amount of suitable impurity, becomes an extrinsic semiconductor. In thermal equilibrium, the electron and hole concentration in it are related to the concentration of intrinsic charge carriers. A p-type or n-type semiconductor can be converted into a p-n junction by doping it with suitable impurity. Two processes, diffusion and drift take place during formation of a p-n junction. A semiconductor diode is basically a p-n junction with metallic contacts provided at the ends for the application of an external voltage. A p-n junction diode allows currents to pass only in one direction when it is forward biased. Due to this property, a diode is widely used to rectify alternating voltages, in half-wave or full wave configuration.
questions.instruction_line: प्रश्न संख्या 29 से 30 केस आधारित प्रश्न हैं । नीचे दिए गए अनुच्छेद का अध्ययन करके प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए ।
questions.instruction_line_english: Questions 29 to 30 are Case Study based questions. Read the following paragraph and answer the questions that follow.

sub_questions.text: जब Ge का मादन पंचसंयोजक अपद्रव्य के साथ किया जाता है, तो अपमिश्रक से दुर्बल-बंध से जुड़े इलेक्ट्रॉन को मुक्त कराने के लिए आवश्यक ऊर्जा होती है लगभग
sub_questions.text_english: When Ge is doped with pentavalent impurity, the energy required to free the weakly bound electron from the dopant is about
sub_questions.solution: When Ge is doped with a pentavalent impurity (donor), the extra electron from the donor atom is very loosely bound to the impurity atom. The ionisation energy required to free this electron is very small, approximately 0.01 eV, which is much less than the band gap of Ge (0.72 eV). Option (B) is correct. Option (A) 0.001 eV is too small; options (C) and (D) correspond to band gaps of Ge and Si respectively, not the donor ionisation energy.

sub_questions.text: किसी दिए गए ताप पर किसी अर्धचालक में नैज आवेश वाहकों की संख्या 2.0 × 10¹⁰ cm⁻³ है । इसका मादन पंचसंयोजक अपद्रव्यी परमाणुओं से किया गया है । इसके परिणामस्वरूप इसमें विवरों (होलों) की संख्या 8 × 10³ cm⁻³ हो जाती है । इस अर्धचालक में इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या है
sub_questions.text_english: At a given temperature, the number of intrinsic charge carriers in a semiconductor is 2.0 × 10¹⁰ cm⁻³. It is doped with pentavalent impurity atoms. As a result, the number of holes in it becomes 8 × 10³ cm⁻³. The number of electrons in the semiconductor is
sub_questions.solution: Using the mass action law: nₑ × nₕ = nᵢ². Given nᵢ = 2.0 × 10¹⁰ cm⁻³ and nₕ = 8 × 10³ cm⁻³, we get nₑ = nᵢ²/nₕ = (2.0 × 10¹⁰)²/(8 × 10³) = (4 × 10²⁰)/(8 × 10³) = 5 × 10¹⁶ cm⁻³ = 5 × 10²² m⁻³. Option (D) is correct.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कोई एक उत्तर दीजिए : (a) किसी p-n संधि के बनते समय —
sub_questions.text_english: Attempt any one: (a) During the formation of a p-n junction –

options.A: electrons diffuse from p-region into n-region and holes diffuse from n-region into p-region.
options.B: both electrons and holes diffuse from n-region into p-region.
options.C: electrons diffuse from n-region into p-region and holes diffuse from p-region into n-region.
options.D: both electrons and holes diffuse from p-region into n-region.

options_english.A: electrons diffuse from p-region into n-region and holes diffuse from n-region into p-region.
options_english.B: both electrons and holes diffuse from n-region into p-region.
options_english.C: electrons diffuse from n-region into p-region and holes diffuse from p-region into n-region.
options_english.D: both electrons and holes diffuse from p-region into n-region.

sub_questions.solution: During the formation of a p-n junction, diffusion occurs due to the concentration gradient. Electrons (majority carriers in n-region) diffuse from the n-region into the p-region, and holes (majority carriers in p-region) diffuse from the p-region into the n-region. This is option (C). Options (A), (B), and (D) describe incorrect directions of diffusion.

sub_questions.text: (b) किसी p-n संधि के बनते समय आरम्भ में —
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Initially during the formation of a p-n junction –

options.A: diffusion current is large and drift current is small.
options.B: diffusion current is small and drift current is large.
options.C: both the diffusion and the drift currents are large.
options.D: both the diffusion and the drift currents are small.

options_english.A: diffusion current is large and drift current is small.
options_english.B: diffusion current is small and drift current is large.
options_english.C: both the diffusion and the drift currents are large.
options_english.D: both the diffusion and the drift currents are small.

sub_questions.solution: Initially, when the p-n junction is just being formed, there is a large concentration gradient of electrons and holes across the junction. This drives a large diffusion current (electrons diffusing to p-side, holes to n-side). At this stage, the depletion region and the built-in electric field have not yet developed significantly, so the drift current due to minority carriers is very small. Hence option (A) is correct.

sub_questions.text: किसी ac वोल्टता V = 0.5 sin (100 πt) वोल्ट को बारी-बारी से किसी अर्ध तरंग दिष्टकारी तथा पूर्ण तरंग दिष्टकारी के सिरों से संयोजित किया गया है । इनके सिरों पर निर्गत वोल्टता की आवृत्ति क्रमशः होगी
sub_questions.text_english: An ac voltage V = 0.5 sin (100 πt) volt is applied, in turn, across a half-wave rectifier and a full-wave rectifier. The frequency of the output voltage across them respectively will be
sub_questions.solution: The input ac voltage is V = 0.5 sin(100πt), so the input frequency is f = 100π/(2π) = 50 Hz. In a half-wave rectifier, only one half-cycle is passed per complete input cycle, so the output frequency equals the input frequency = 50 Hz. In a full-wave rectifier, both half-cycles are utilised (each rectified), so the output has twice as many pulses per second as the input, giving output frequency = 2 × 50 = 100 Hz. Therefore the frequencies are 50 Hz and 100 Hz respectively. Option (D) is correct.

questions.text: कोई लेंस दो पृष्ठों से घिरा ऐसा पारदर्शी प्रकाशिक माध्यम होता है जिसके दोनों पृष्ठों में कम से कम एक गोलीय होना चाहिए । किसी एकल गोलीय पृष्ठ द्वारा निर्मित प्रतिबिम्ब के लिए सूत्र का उपयोग किसी लेंस के दो पृष्ठों पर क्रमिक रूप से करके पतले लेंसों के लिए लेंस सूत्र जिसे लेंस मेकर सूत्र और इस प्रकार मूल लेंस सूत्र प्राप्त किया जाता है । किसी लेंस की फोकस दूरी (अथवा क्षमता) लेंस के दोनों पृष्ठों की त्रिज्याओं तथा प्रतिवेश के सापेक्ष लेंस के पदार्थ के अपवर्तनांक पर निर्भर करता है । किसी पदार्थ का अपवर्तनांक उपयोग किए गए प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्घ्य पर निर्भर करता है । लेंसों का संयोजन वांछित क्षमता और आवर्धन के अपसारी और अभिसारी लेंसों को प्राप्त करने में हमारी सहायता करता है ।
questions.text_english: A lens is a transparent optical medium bounded by two surfaces; at least one of which should be spherical. Applying the formula of image formation by a single spherical surface successively at the two surfaces of a thin lens, a formula known as lens maker's formula and hence the basic lens formula can be obtained. The focal length (or power) of a lens depends on the radii of its surfaces and the refractive index of its material with respect to the surrounding medium. The refractive index of a material depends on the wavelength of light used. Combination of lenses helps us to obtain diverging or converging lenses of desired power and magnification.

sub_questions.text: 20 cm फोकस दूरी का कोई पतला अपसारी लेंस 15 cm फोकस दूरी के पतले अभिसारी लेंस के सम्पर्क में समाक्ष रखा है । इस संयोजन की क्षमता है –
sub_questions.text_english: A thin converging lens of focal length 20 cm and a thin diverging lens of focal length 15 cm are placed coaxially in contact. The power of the combination is
sub_questions.solution: Power of converging lens P₁ = 100/f₁ = 100/20 = +5 D. Power of diverging lens P₂ = 100/f₂ = 100/(–15) = –20/3 D. Combined power P = P₁ + P₂ = 5 – 20/3 = 15/3 – 20/3 = –5/3 D. Option (B) is correct.

sub_questions.text: किसी उत्तल लेंस के दो पृष्ठों की वक्रता त्रिज्या R और 2R हैं । यदि इस लेंस की फोकस दूरी (4/3)R है, तो लेंस के पदार्थ का अपवर्तनांक है :
sub_questions.text_english: The radii of curvature of two surfaces of a convex lens are R and 2R. If the focal length of this lens is (4/3)R, the refractive index of the material of the lens is :
sub_questions.solution: Using the Lens Maker's formula: 1/f = (n–1)[1/R₁ – 1/R₂]. For a convex lens with R₁ = R (first surface, positive) and R₂ = –2R (second surface, negative for convex): 1/f = (n–1)[1/R – 1/(–2R)] = (n–1)[1/R + 1/2R] = (n–1)(3/2R). Given f = (4/3)R: 1/[(4/3)R] = (n–1)(3/2R) → 3/(4R) = 3(n–1)/(2R) → n–1 = 1/2 → n = 3/2. Option (C) is correct.

sub_questions.text: किसी समतलोत्तल लेंस की फोकस दूरी
sub_questions.text_english: The focal length of an equiconvex lens

options.A: पानी में डुबोने पर बढ़ जाती है । / increases when the lens is dipped in water.
options.B: आपतित प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्घ्य में कमी होने पर बढ़ जाती है । / increases when the wavelength of incident light decreases.
options.C: इसके पृष्ठों की वक्रता त्रिज्या में कमी होने पर बढ़ जाती है । / increases with decrease in radius of curvature of its surface.
options.D: मुख्य अक्ष के अनुदिश दो सर्वसम भागों में काटे जाने पर घट जाती है । / decreases when the lens is cut into two identical parts along its principal axis.

options_english.A: increases when the lens is dipped in water.
options_english.B: increases when the wavelength of incident light decreases.
options_english.C: increases with decrease in radius of curvature of its surface.
options_english.D: decreases when the lens is cut into two identical parts along its principal axis.

sub_questions.solution: When a glass lens is dipped in water, the refractive index of glass relative to water (n_glass/n_water ≈ 1.5/1.33 ≈ 1.13) is much less than relative to air (1.5). Since f = R/(2(n–1)) for an equiconvex lens, a smaller (n–1) means a larger focal length. So dipping in water increases focal length. Option (A) is correct. Option (B) is wrong because decreasing wavelength increases refractive index (n increases), reducing focal length. Option (C) is wrong: decreasing R decreases f. Option (D) is wrong: cutting along the principal axis gives two plano-convex lenses each with the same focal length as the original.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कोई एक उत्तर दीजिए : (a) आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार 10 cm फोकस दूरी का कोई उत्तल पतला लेंस L और 15 cm फोकस दूरी का कोई अवतल दर्पण M एक-दूसरे से 40 cm की दूरी पर समाक्ष स्थित हैं । मुख्य अक्ष से समान्तर कोई प्रकाश पुन्ज लेंस पर आपतन करता है । अंतिम प्रतिबिम्ब लेंस के सापेक्ष कहाँ और कितनी दूरी पर बनेगा ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) A thin convex lens L of focal length 10 cm and a concave mirror M of focal length 15 cm are placed coaxially 40 cm apart as shown in figure. A beam of light coming parallel to the principal axis is incident on the lens. The final image will be formed at a distance of
sub_questions.solution: Parallel rays from infinity hit the convex lens (f = 10 cm) and converge at its focal point, 10 cm to the right of the lens. This point is 40 – 10 = 30 cm in front of the concave mirror (f = 15 cm). Using the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, with u = –30 cm, f = –15 cm: 1/v = 1/(–15) – 1/(–30) = –1/15 + 1/30 = –2/30 + 1/30 = –1/30, giving v = –30 cm. So the image after the mirror is 30 cm in front of the mirror. This image is 40 – 30 = 10 cm to the left of the lens. The final image is 10 cm to the left of the lens. Option (A) is correct.

sub_questions.text: (b) 16 cm फोकस दूरी के किसी उत्तल लेंस L₁ पर कोई प्रकाश पुन्ज, जो लेंस के मुख्य अक्ष के समान्तर है, आपतन कर रहा है । लेंस L₁ के समाक्ष कोई अन्य उत्तल लेंस L₂ जिसकी फोकस दूरी 12 cm है, 40 cm दूरी पर स्थित है । अंतिम प्रतिबिम्ब की प्रकृति और लेंस L₂ से दूरी होगी क्रमश:
sub_questions.text_english: (b) A beam of light coming parallel to the principal axis of a convex lens L₁ of focal length 16 cm is incident on it. Another convex lens L₂ of focal length 12 cm is placed coaxially at a distance 40 cm from L₁. The nature and distance of the final image from L₂ will be
sub_questions.solution: Parallel rays on L₁ (f₁ = 16 cm) converge at 16 cm to the right of L₁. This point is 40 – 16 = 24 cm to the right of L₁ but 40 – 16 = 24 cm means the intermediate image is 24 cm ahead of L₂ (since L₂ is 40 cm from L₁, and the image is at 16 cm from L₁, so it is 40 – 16 = 24 cm to the left of L₂). Using lens formula for L₂: u = –24 cm, f₂ = +12 cm → 1/v = 1/12 + 1/(–24) wait: 1/v – 1/u = 1/f → 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/12 + 1/(–24) = 2/24 – 1/24 = 1/24. So v = 24 cm to the right of L₂. The image is real (positive v) and 24 cm from L₂. Option (A) is correct.

questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से कोई एक भाग हल कीजिए ।
questions.instruction_line_english: Attempt any one of the following parts.

sub_questions.text:
(i) किसी उत्तल दर्पण द्वारा किसी बिम्ब का प्रतिबिम्ब बनना दर्शाने के लिए किरण आरेख खींचिए और इससे दर्पण समीकरण प्राप्त कीजिए ।
(ii) प्रकाशिक यंत्रों के अभिदृश्यक और अभिनेत्र लेंस (नेत्रिका) दोनों के लिए बहुघटक लेंसों का उपयोग क्यों किया जाता है ?
(iii) किसी संयुक्त सूक्ष्मदर्शी द्वारा किसी लघु बिम्ब का आवर्धन 200 है । नेत्रिका की फोकस दूरी 2 cm है तथा अंतिम प्रतिबिम्ब अनन्त पर बनता है । अभिदृश्यक द्वारा उत्पन्न आवर्धन ज्ञात कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
(i) Draw a ray diagram for the formation of the image of an object by a convex mirror. Hence, obtain the mirror equation.
(ii) Why are multi-component lenses used for both the objective and the eyepiece in optical instruments ?
(iii) The magnification of a small object produced by a compound microscope is 200. The focal length of the eyepiece is 2 cm and the final image is formed at infinity. Find the magnification produced by the objective.

key_points: (i) Ray diagram with derivation of 1/v + 1/u = 1/f for convex mirror using similar triangles.
(ii) Multi-component lenses correct aberrations (chromatic and spherical aberration).
(iii) M_e = 1 + D/f_e = 1 + 25/2 = 13.5 (but for image at infinity M_e = D/f_e = 25/2 = 12.5); M_o = M/M_e = 200/12.5 = 16.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) In the ray diagram for a convex mirror, an object AB is placed in front. Two rays are drawn: (a) a ray parallel to the principal axis, which after reflection appears to diverge from the focal point F behind the mirror; (b) a ray directed toward the centre of curvature C, which reflects back along the same path. The two reflected rays, when produced behind the mirror, meet at A', forming a virtual, erect, and diminished image A'B'. From the geometry of similar triangles, we derive: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, which is the mirror equation (using the standard sign convention).
(ii) Multi-component (compound) lenses are used in optical instruments to minimise aberrations — specifically chromatic aberration (where different wavelengths focus at different points) and spherical aberration (where rays from the periphery focus at different points from paraxial rays). A combination of lenses of different materials and curvatures can correct both types of aberrations simultaneously.
(iii) For a compound microscope with the final image at infinity, the magnification of the eyepiece is M_e = D/f_e = 25/2 = 12.5 (where D = 25 cm is the least distance of distinct vision). Total magnification M = M_o × M_e → 200 = M_o × 12.5 → M_o = 200/12.5 = 16. The magnification produced by the objective is 16.

sub_questions.text:
(i) किसी तरंगाग्र और किसी किरण के बीच विभेदन कीजिए ।
(ii) हाइगेन्स सिद्धान्त लिखिए तथा उपयुक्त आरेख का उपयोग करके परावर्तन के नियमों का सत्यापन कीजिए ।
(iii) यंग के द्विझिरी प्रयोग में झिरियों S₁ और S₂ के बीच की दूरी 3 mm है तथा पर्दे की झिरियों से दूरी 1.0 m है । यह प्रेक्षण किया गया है कि चौथी चमकीली फ्रिंज दूसरी काली फ्रिंज से 5 mm की दूरी पर है । उपयोग किए जाने वाले प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्घ्य ज्ञात कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
(i) Differentiate between a wavefront and a ray.
(ii) State Huygen's principle and verify laws of reflection using suitable diagram.
(iii) In Young's double slit experiment, the slits S₁ and S₂ are 3 mm apart and the screen is placed 1.0 m away from the slits. It is observed that the fourth bright fringe is at a distance of 5 mm from the second dark fringe. Find the wavelength of light used.

key_points: (i) Wavefront: locus of all points oscillating in same phase; ray: direction of propagation of wave energy, perpendicular to wavefront.
(ii) Huygens principle: every point on a wavefront acts as a secondary source of wavelets; new wavefront is the common tangent to all secondary wavelets. Used to derive laws of reflection.
(iii) Position of nth bright fringe: y_n = nλD/d; Position of nth dark fringe: y_n = (2n–1)λD/(2d); 4th bright – 2nd dark = 5 mm → λ = 0.6 μm.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) A wavefront is the locus of all points in a medium that are in the same phase of oscillation at a given instant. It is always perpendicular to the direction of propagation of the wave. A ray is a line drawn in the direction of propagation of the wave energy, always perpendicular to the wavefront.
(ii) Huygens' Principle states: (a) Every point on a given wavefront acts as a fresh source of secondary wavelets that spread out in all directions with the speed of the wave in that medium. (b) The new wavefront at any later time is the forward common tangent (envelope) to all the secondary wavelets. For reflection: Consider a plane wavefront AB incident on a plane mirror at an angle i. Point A touches the mirror and sends out a secondary wavelet of radius ct (where t is the time for the wavefront to travel from B to B'). The reflected wavefront A'B' is the common tangent to this wavelet. By geometry, triangles ABB' and AA'B' are congruent (AB = A'B' = ct), proving that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
(iii) In Young's double slit experiment: d = 3 mm = 3×10⁻³ m, D = 1.0 m. Position of 4th bright fringe: y₄ = 4λD/d. Position of 2nd dark fringe: y₂_dark = (2×2–1)λD/(2d) = 3λD/(2d). Distance between 4th bright and 2nd dark = y₄ – y₂_dark = 4λD/d – 3λD/(2d) = (8λD – 3λD)/(2d) = 5λD/(2d) = 5 mm. So λ = (5×10⁻³ × 2 × 3×10⁻³)/(5 × 1.0) = (30×10⁻⁶)/5 = 6×10⁻⁶ m... let me recalculate: 5λD/(2d) = 5×10⁻³ → λ = (5×10⁻³ × 2d)/(5D) = (2×3×10⁻³)/(1.0) × 10⁻³ = 6×10⁻⁶/5... Actually: λ = (5×10⁻³ × 2 × 3×10⁻³)/(5 × 1.0) = 6×10⁻⁷ m = 600 nm = 0.6 μm.

sub_questions.text:
(i) किसी समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र जिसकी पट्टिकाओं के बीच पृथकन d तथा पट्टिकाओं का क्षेत्रफल A है, की पट्टिकाओं के बीच परावैद्युतांक 'K' और मोटाई 't' का कोई गुटका रखा गया है । इस संधारित्र की धारिता के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए ।
(ii) दो विभिन्न धारिताओं के संधारित्रों को पहले (1) श्रेणी में और फिर (2) पार्श्व में किसी 100 V के dc स्रोत से संयोजित किया गया है । यदि इन दोनों प्रकरणों में संयोजनों में संचित कुल ऊर्जा क्रमशः 40 mJ और 250 mJ हैं, तो इन संधारित्रों की धारिताएँ ज्ञात कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
(i) A dielectric slab of dielectric constant 'K' and thickness 't' is inserted between plates of a parallel plate capacitor of plate separation d and plate area A. Obtain an expression for its capacitance.
(ii) Two capacitors of different capacitances are connected first (1) in series and then (2) in parallel across a dc source of 100 V. If the total energy stored in the combination in the two cases are 40 mJ and 250 mJ respectively, find the capacitance of the capacitors.

key_points: (i) C = ε₀A/(d – t + t/K)

(ii) Series: C_s = C₁C₂/(C₁+C₂); E_s = ½C_s V² = 40 mJ → C_s = 8 μF. Parallel: C_p = C₁+C₂; E_p = ½C_p V² = 250 mJ → C_p = 50 μF. Solving C₁+C₂=50, C₁C₂/(C₁+C₂)=8 → C₁C₂=400 → C₁,C₂ = 10 μF and 40 μF.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) When a dielectric slab of constant K and thickness t is inserted between plates (separation d, area A), the effective gap has two air gaps of total thickness (d–t) and a dielectric gap of thickness t. These act as capacitors in series: C_air = ε₀A/(d–t) and C_dielectric = Kε₀A/t. The combined capacitance is C = ε₀A/(d – t + t/K).
(ii) Let C₁ and C₂ be the two capacitances and V = 100 V. In series: C_s = C₁C₂/(C₁+C₂); energy E_s = ½C_s V² = 40×10⁻³ J → C_s = 2×40×10⁻³/100² = 8×10⁻⁶ F = 8 μF. In parallel: C_p = C₁+C₂; energy E_p = ½C_p V² = 250×10⁻³ J → C_p = 2×250×10⁻³/100² = 50×10⁻⁶ F = 50 μF. So C₁+C₂ = 50 μF and C₁C₂/(C₁+C₂) = 8 μF → C₁C₂ = 8×50 = 400 (μF)². Solving the quadratic: C² – 50C + 400 = 0 → C = (50 ± √(2500–1600))/2 = (50 ± 30)/2. Thus C₁ = 40 μF and C₂ = 10 μF.

sub_questions.text:
(i) गाउस नियम का उपयोग करके यह दर्शाइए कि किसी एकसमान आवेशित अनंत समतल चादर के कारण किसी बिन्दु पर विद्युत क्षेत्र E→ = σ/(2ε₀) n̂ से व्यक्त होता है । यहाँ प्रतीकों के अपने सामान्य अर्थ हैं ।
(ii) किसी प्रदेश में विद्युत क्षेत्र E→ को इस प्रकार व्यक्त किया गया है E→ = (5x² + 2) î, यहाँ E को N/C तथा x को मीटरों में व्यक्त किया गया है । इस प्रदेश में भुजा 10 cm के किसी घन को आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार स्थित किया गया है । परिकलित कीजिए: (1) इस घन से गुजरने वाला विद्युत फ्लक्स, तथा (2) इस घन द्वारा परिबद्ध नेट आवेश ।
sub_questions.text_english:
(i) Using Gauss's law, show that the electric field E→ at a point due to a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet is given by E→ = σ/(2ε₀) n̂ where symbols have their usual meanings.
(ii) Electric field E→ in a region is given by E→ = (5x² + 2) î where E is in N/C and x is in meters. A cube of side 10 cm is placed in the region as shown in figure. Calculate (1) the electric flux through the cube, and (2) the net charge enclosed by the cube.

key_points: (i) Gaussian surface is a cylinder symmetric about the sheet; by Gauss law: E × 2A = σA/ε₀ → E = σ/(2ε₀).

(ii) Flux through face at x=0: E(0) = 2 N/C → Φ₁ = –2×(0.1)² = –0.02 N m²/C (inward); face at x=0.1: E(0.1)=5×0.01+2=2.05 N/C → Φ₂ = 2.05×0.01 = 0.0205 N m²/C (outward); Net flux = 0.0205–0.02 = 0.0005 N m²/C.
Net charge Q = ε₀ × Φ_net = 8.854×10⁻¹² × 5×10⁻⁴ ≈ 4.43×10⁻¹⁵ C.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) Consider an infinite plane sheet with surface charge density σ. By symmetry, the electric field points perpendicular to the sheet on both sides. Draw a cylindrical Gaussian surface of cross-sectional area A passing through the sheet symmetrically. The flux through the curved surface is zero; flux through the two flat ends is E × A + E × A = 2EA. By Gauss's law: 2EA = σA/ε₀ → E = σ/(2ε₀). In vector form: E→ = σ/(2ε₀) n̂, where n̂ is the outward normal.
(ii) The cube has side L = 0.1 m. Place the cube with one face at x = 0 and opposite face at x = 0.1 m. The electric field E = (5x² + 2) î only has an x-component, so only the two faces perpendicular to the x-axis contribute to flux. At x = 0: E = 5(0)² + 2 = 2 N/C; flux through left face (inward): Φ₁ = –2 × (0.1)² = –0.02 N m²/C. At x = 0.1 m: E = 5(0.1)² + 2 = 0.05 + 2 = 2.05 N/C; flux through right face (outward): Φ₂ = +2.05 × (0.1)² = +0.0205 N m²/C. Net flux: Φ_net = 0.0205 – 0.02 = 0.0005 N m²/C = 5 × 10⁻⁴ N m²/C. Net charge enclosed: Q = ε₀ Φ_net = 8.854 × 10⁻¹² × 5 × 10⁻⁴ ≈ 4.43 × 10⁻¹⁵ C.

sub_questions.text:
(i) उन कारकों का उल्लेख कीजिए जिन पर किसी LCR श्रेणी परिपथ की अनुनाद की आवृत्ति निर्भर करती है । अनुप्रयुक्त ac स्रोत की आवृत्ति के साथ LCR श्रेणी परिपथ की प्रतिबाधा में विचरण को दर्शाने के लिए ग्राफ खींचिए ।
(ii) उपयुक्त आरेख की सहायता से किसी उच्चायी ट्रान्सफॉर्मर की कार्यविधि की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
(iii) किसी वास्तविक ट्रान्सफॉर्मर में ऊर्जा-क्षय के दो कारण लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
(i) Mention the factors on which the resonant frequency of a series LCR circuit depends. Plot a graph showing variation of impedance of a series LCR circuit with the frequency of the applied a.c. source.
(ii) With the help of a suitable diagram, explain the working of a step-up transformer.
(iii) Write two causes of energy loss in a real transformer.

key_points: (i) Resonant frequency f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)); depends on L (inductance) and C (capacitance); impedance minimum at resonance.
(ii) Step-up transformer: N_s > N_p; V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p > 1; works on mutual induction; primary AC → changing flux → induced EMF in secondary.
(iii) Energy losses: (a) Copper (Joule heating) loss — due to resistance of windings; (b) Iron/core losses — eddy currents and hysteresis in the iron core.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) The resonant frequency of a series LCR circuit is f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)). It depends on the inductance L and capacitance C of the circuit; it does not depend on resistance R. The graph of impedance Z versus frequency f shows a U-shaped curve: Z is large at both very low and very high frequencies, and reaches a minimum value equal to R at the resonant frequency f₀.
(ii) A step-up transformer increases voltage. It consists of a primary coil of N_p turns and a secondary coil of N_s turns (N_s > N_p) wound on a laminated soft iron core. When an alternating voltage V_p is applied to the primary, it creates a time-varying magnetic flux in the core. By Faraday's law, this changing flux induces an EMF in the secondary: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p. Since N_s > N_p, V_s > V_p (voltage is stepped up). By energy conservation, I_p V_p = I_s V_s, so current decreases as voltage increases.
(iii) Two causes of energy loss in a real transformer: (a) Copper loss (Joule heating): the primary and secondary coils have some resistance, so current flowing through them dissipates energy as heat (I²R loss). (b) Iron core losses: (i) Eddy current losses — the changing magnetic flux induces circulating currents (eddy currents) in the iron core that produce heat; minimised by using laminated cores. (ii) Hysteresis loss — energy is wasted in repeatedly magnetising and demagnetising the iron core; minimised by using soft iron with narrow hysteresis loop.

sub_questions.text:
(i) आरेख की सहायता से किसी ac जनित्र की संरचना और कार्यविधि की संक्षेप में व्याख्या कीजिए ।
(ii) कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन किसी प्रोटॉन की परिक्रमा त्रिज्या r की कक्षा में चाल v से कर रहा है । इस इलेक्ट्रॉन से संबद्ध चुम्बकीय आघूर्ण के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
(i) With the help of a diagram, briefly explain the construction and working of ac generator.
(ii) An electron is revolving around a proton in an orbit of radius r with a speed v. Obtain expression for magnetic moment associated with the electron.

key_points: (i) AC generator: rotating coil in magnetic field; EMF ε = NBAω sin(ωt); slip rings and brushes collect current.
(ii) Current due to electron: I = ev/(2πr); magnetic moment μ = IA = ev/(2πr) × πr² = evr/2.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) An AC generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy using electromagnetic induction. Construction: it consists of a rectangular coil ABCD of N turns wound on an armature, placed in a strong uniform magnetic field B. Two slip rings are connected to the ends of the coil, and two carbon brushes press against the slip rings to collect the current. Working: when the armature rotates with angular velocity ω, the magnetic flux through the coil changes as Φ = NBA cos(ωt). By Faraday's law, the induced EMF is ε = –dΦ/dt = NBAω sin(ωt) = ε₀ sin(ωt), where ε₀ = NBAω is the peak EMF. This sinusoidally varying EMF is delivered to the external circuit through the brushes and slip rings.
(ii) An electron revolving around a proton in an orbit of radius r with speed v completes one revolution in time T = 2πr/v. The equivalent electric current is I = e/T = ev/(2πr). The magnetic moment associated with a current loop is μ = I × A, where A = πr² is the area of the orbit. Therefore μ = ev/(2πr) × πr² = evr/2. The direction of the magnetic moment is opposite to the angular momentum of the electron (since the electron is negatively charged).
